# Refactor: decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` (1,132 lines)

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — 1,132 lines.

## Problem statement

The worklist mouse-input test suite exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability
ceiling (~1,132 lines) and should be decomposed so that no test file exceeds the
ceiling.

## Goal

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No file exceeds 1,000 lines.
2. All imports still resolve; all existing tests pass without modification to
   their assertions (move-only refactor).
3. No new circular imports.
4. All related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate test groups and update imports; do not change test
  assertions or test logic.
- **Test-file scope.** This item exists because the producer declined to include
  test-file decomposition in WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B (intake Q1 → answer A):
  "production modules only; tests stay unmodified as the behaviour gate and a
  follow-up item is filed for the two oversized suites."
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B** — *Decompose packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts god class*
  (parent epic; discovered-from intake Q1 → answer A).

## Sequencing & validation (added at plan time, WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B)

- **Prerequisite:** `WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N` (finalise the production barrel) — the
  production split must land first; splitting these tests against a moving
  barrel would churn imports twice.
- **Test-first gate:** the worklist split guard
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`, `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J`)
  already asserts every production module ≤1,000 lines. Extend the same guard
  (or add a sibling guard) to assert every `worklist*.test.ts` file is ≤1,000
  lines once this item lands.
- **Move-only:** relocate describe blocks and their imports; assertions and test
  names stay byte-identical. Import from concrete `worklist.*.js` module paths
  only where the barrel does not expose an internal symbol — never from
  `index.ts`.
- **Validation:** `tsc --noEmit`/build, split guard green, and the full
  `packages/herdr` suite green (`/skill:test`).

# Decompose `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (4,284 lines)

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 (Refactor: decompose
`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module).
**Status:** follow-up, deliberately **outside** that epic.

## Why this is not part of the index.ts epic

The index.ts split (WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6) is a move-only refactor whose
behaviour gate is that `index.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts` and
`fetchAuditItemById.test.ts` stay **byte-identical**. Decomposing
`index.test.ts` inside the same epic would erase that signal, so it is filed
here as a separate item (plan decision Q3 → A).

## Target outcome

`packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (4,284 lines, measured 2026-11-05) is split
into cohesive test modules grouped by the production module they exercise
(commands, args, pane-capture, background, interactive/resolvers,
downtime-deps, settings/main) or another agreed grouping, with no test cases
lost and no production-code changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wc -l` reports ≤ 1,000 lines for every resulting `index*.test.ts` module.
- The total number of test cases (`it(`/`test(`) and assertions is unchanged before and after; no test is deleted, skipped or weakened.
- No production module changes; `packages/herdr` build and full test suite pass.
- Shared fixtures/helpers are extracted into a single helper module rather than duplicated across the new files.
- The split guard's line-ceiling gate excludes test files (asserted explicitly) so test sizes are not policed by the production ceiling.

## Baseline metrics (measured 2026-11-05 on `dev` @ 33bd3a07)

AC1/AC2 are verified against these numbers before and after the split:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — **4,284 lines**; 34 top-level
  `describe` blocks (41 including nested); **226 `it(...)` declarations** plus
  one `it.each` table with 4 parameterised cases (**231 executed cases**);
  **400 `expect(...)` assertions**; 4 `beforeEach`, 15 `afterEach`.
- No `it.skip`, `it.only` or `test(` call exists today; none may be added.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` — 484 lines (already under the
  ceiling and otherwise untouched apart from the AC5 assertion).

## Grouping map (inventory, measured 2026-11-05)

| Proposed module | Describes it takes (start line → length) | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `index.args.test.ts` | `buildSendToPiArgs` (72→103), `buildRunInPaneArgs` (175→100), item-tab anchor variants (275→43, 318→69), pane-id capture flag (3436→26), request priority (4005→24) | ~365 |
| `index.interactive.test.ts` | `extractWorkItemId` (387→17), `resolveInteractiveWorkspaceId` (404→30), `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (434→116), `defaultInteractiveLiveTrackedPanesResolver` (550→93), `closeInteractiveTabRootPane` (643→123), `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority` (4111→86), operator-dispatch chain (4197→87) | ~552 |
| `index.commands.test.ts` | `stripCommandPrefix` (766→116), shortcuts.json routing (882→119), `routeCommand` (1001→56), `stripAgentPromptPrefix` (1057→48) | ~339 |
| `index.pane-capture.test.ts` | `parsePaneIdFile` (3462→17), `capturePaneIdFromFile` (3479→85) | ~128 |
| `index.background.test.ts` | `buildBackgroundLogPath` (3629→14), `spawnBackgroundShell` (3643→64), `formatBackgroundFailure` (3707→44), `spawnBackgroundPi` (3751→57), `spawnBackgroundPi` priority env (4029→82) | ~261 |
| `index.settings.test.ts` | `configureWorklogTarget` (1105→108) | ~108 |
| `index.downtime-deps*.test.ts` | `createDowntimeDeps` (1213→**1,407**), `host-wide audit admission` (2620→380), `recordDispatch` (3000→161), `recordError` (3161→37), `recordDispatchFailure` (3198→83), `getDueScheduledPrompt` (3281→89), `recordScheduledPromptTrigger` (3370→66), `rotation wiring` (3564→65) | ~2,288 |
| `index.stalled-work-wiring.test.ts` | `stalled-work production wiring` (3808→197) | ~197 |

Consequences of the inventory:

- The single `createDowntimeDeps` describe (**1,407 lines**) cannot move into one
  module under AC1. It must be subdivided by its nested describes (or at a
  shared-setup seam) so that the downtime-deps family lands in at least three
  modules ≤ 1,000 lines each, with `createDowntimeDeps` setup in
  `index.fixtures.ts`.
- The 2,288-line downtime-deps family is the bulk of the work; the remaining
  ~1,750 lines split cleanly by production module.

## Minimal implementation

1. Inventory done — see **Grouping map** above (verify it still matches before
   moving code; the file grows over time).
2. Extract shared mocks/fixtures to `packages/herdr/src/index.fixtures.ts`
   (suite-wide `beforeEach`/`afterEach` host-CPU pinning, `makeInteractiveAnchorDeps`,
   `loadInteractiveAnchorHelpers`, `createDowntimeDeps` stubs and other shared
   arrange helpers).
3. Move blocks into `index.<concern>.test.ts` files; keep imports pointing at
   `./index.js` (the barrel) so the public-surface contract keeps being tested.
   Import a concrete `./index.<slice>.js` path only where the barrel does not
   expose the symbol.
4. Add the explicit AC5 assertion to `index.split-guard.test.ts`: test/fixture
   files are excluded from the production line ceiling (today that exclusion is
   only implicit in `productionModules()` filtering).
5. Update `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/dispatcher-anchor-family.ts`
   `KNOWN_CONSUMER_FILES` (it names `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, and
   `findBarrelConsumers(...)` is asserted to equal the list exactly) to name the
   module that keeps the `DispatcherAnchorDeps` type imports.
6. Verify with `/skill:test` scoped to `packages/herdr`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — source of the split (4,284 lines).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.*.test.ts` — new test modules.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.fixtures.ts` — shared fixtures (new).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` — receives the AC5 assertion.
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/dispatcher-anchor-family.ts` — frozen
  consumer list update (test tooling, not a production module).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate `describe` blocks, helpers and imports; test names and
  assertions stay byte-identical. No test deleted, skipped, renamed or weakened.
- **Test-only change;** must not alter production behaviour or public surface.
  `packages/herdr/src/index.split-baseline.json` is a frozen contract — never
  regenerate it to make a gate green.
- **Fixture naming matters.** `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`'s
  `isTestOrFixture()` recognises only `*.test.ts` and `*.fixtures.ts`, while
  `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN` (`/^index(\.[\w-]+)?\.ts$/`) *does* match
  `index.test-helpers.ts` — so a helper named `index.test-helpers.ts` would be
  treated as an index-family **production** module and held to the 1,000-line
  ceiling plus the single-declaration/single-callsite gates. Use
  `index.fixtures.ts`, matching the existing `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` /
  `host-dispatch-budget.fixtures.ts` convention.
- **Do not pollute the production size gate.** `INDEX_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` and
  `INDEX_SPLIT_ALLOWLIST_CEILING` are `['index.ts']` and shrink-only; no split
  test module may be added to them.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf test groups first, keeping the
  tree green between moves; run the scoped suite after each module.
- **Guard divergence is deliberate.** The sibling test-decomposition items
  (`WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L`, `WL-0MVHUU096008OQSW`) extend their split guard to
  *police* `worklist*.test.ts` at ≤1,000 lines; this item's AC5 requires the
  opposite for the index family (test files explicitly **excluded** from the
  production ceiling). Do not harmonise the two.
- **No production-split prerequisite.** `index.ts` is still 2,072 lines and
  remains on the shrink-only allowlist; its epic (WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6) is
  deleted, so this item is independent. Moves must not touch `index.ts` itself.

## Related work

- WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 — parent epic (deleted; the split shipped as separate
  production modules and `index.ts` remains on the allowlist).
- WL-0MVHURHZI000CS5L — decompose `worklist.test.ts` (7,073 lines), blocked.
- WL-0MVHUU096008OQSW — decompose `worklist-mouse.test.ts` (1,132 lines), blocked.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.split-guard.test.ts` / `index.split-baseline.json` —
  the structural gates that must stay green.

## Appendix: planning questions, findings and answers

**Duplicate check.** `wl search "index.test.ts"`,
`wl search "decompose test god file split module herdr"` and
`wl search "index.test.ts decompose split test"` performed 2026-11-05. The only
overlapping items are the sibling *worklist* test decompositions (different
files, no AC overlap) and this item; no completed item satisfies these ACs.
**No overlapping completed item found** — proceed.

- **Q: Is `index.test-helpers.ts` (named in the original Key Files) a safe
  fixture name?** Answer (plan, verified against
  `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/{scan,index-family}.ts` with `tsx`):
  **no** — it matches `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN` and is not recognised by
  `isTestOrFixture()`, so it would be gated as production. Accepted naming:
  `index.fixtures.ts`. Evidence: `INDEX_FAMILY_PATTERN.test('index.test-helpers.ts') === true`,
  `isTestOrFixture('index.test-helpers.ts') === false`.
- **Q: Does the line-count in the title/description still hold?** Answer
  (measured): no — the file is 4,284 lines, not 3,990. Title and description
  corrected; counts recorded under **Baseline metrics**.
- **Q: Does the item stay clear of the frozen production gates?** Answer
  (verified): yes, provided the split does not add test modules to the
  allowlist, does not regenerate `index.split-baseline.json`, and updates the
  *test-tooling* `KNOWN_CONSUMER_FILES` list, which currently names
  `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and is asserted by exact equality.
- **Q: Is `claim` a real group in this file (the original description listed
  it)?** Answer (inventory): no — `claim` coverage lives in `claim.test.ts`;
  removed from the grouping list.
- **Decision (scope sizing / phasing):** no children are created and no
  phasing is needed — this is a single move-only deliverable. If the 1,407-line
  `createDowntimeDeps` describe proves unmanageable during implementation,
  `implement` may create children then, test-first (AC5 assertion → fixture
  module → downtime-deps sub-split → remaining concerns).
- **Decision (residual barrel test file):** `index.test.ts` is expected to be
  removed once its describes are distributed; the public-surface contract is
  preserved by the split-guard baseline and by the new modules importing
  `./index.js`. A thin residual `index.test.ts` is acceptable if a home is
  needed for file-level setup.
- **Note (effort/risk provenance):** the autoplan pre-check ran
  `effort-and-risk` with its zeroed placeholder payload (`o=m=p=0`) and wrote
  `Extra Small`/`Low`; step 8 replaced both fields with a real three-point
  estimate (see the effort/risk fields and the `effort_and_risk_skill`
  comment).

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 30 + shared 13 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

**Note:** file counts have grown since the work item was created — `packages/tui` now has 30 test files (was 22) and `packages/shared` has 13 (was 12). The `packages/herdr` count is 129, unchanged. Repository total: 453 test files (up from 440).

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 30 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 13 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **453** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (30 files, all under `packages/tui/extensions/`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (13 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them. (Note: a `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`.)

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

## Existing state

The canonical suite is a single command: `npm --silent test -- tests` (277 files, ~791 s vitest duration, ~1065 s wall clock). The `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`. There is no group for `packages/shared`.

## Desired change

Add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to the canonical full suite coverage. The simplest approach is to add additional commands to `suiteCommands`:

```jsonc
{
  "suiteCommands": [
    "npm --silent test -- tests",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/shared",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/tui/extensions"
  ]
}
```

This adds two positional filters that are precise: `packages/shared` matches only the 13 shared test files, and `packages/tui/extensions` matches only the 30 tui test files (all under `extensions/`), neither of which would match `packages/herdr`.

Alternatively, create named groups (`shared`, `tui`) and wire them into `suiteCommands` as separate commands — same effect, but with changed-scope selection benefits.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to `suiteCommands` (or create named groups + wire them)
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update the coverage table and runtime section
- `vitest.config.ts` — no change expected; existing config handles `packages/` correctly

## Related work

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** — closed the `tests/` coverage gap (umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`); records the OPEN QUESTION that became this item.
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — herdr package suite excluded by producer decision (won't-fix).
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json`.
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — source of the additional-gap evidence for `packages/tui/extensions/**`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should packages/herdr be included?" — Answer (work item description): No — producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix. Source: work item description.
- Q: "What about the `tui-extensions` group that already exists?" — Answer: It is not wired into `suiteCommands`, so it provides no full-suite gate coverage. The brief proposes wiring it (or creating an equivalent group) into suiteCommands. Source: inspection of `.pi/test-config.json`.
- Q: "File counts have changed since the work item was created — should we update the title?" — Answer: Yes — the title should be updated to reflect current counts (30 + 13, not 22 + 12). Source: `git ls-files` on current tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Runtime increase (medium).** Adding 43 files to the canonical suite increases wall-clock. *Mitigation:* measure before/after with `run_tests.py`; `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s, so there is headroom.
- **New coverage may surface pre-existing failures (medium).** Neither `packages/tui` nor `packages/shared` has run under the canonical gate, so latent failures could appear. *Mitigation:* triage into `test-failure` items (AC3).
- **Filter precision (low).** `packages/shared` and `packages/tui/extensions` are substring filters; verified against `git ls-files` that they match only the intended 13 + 30 files and not `packages/herdr`. *Assumption:* `packages/tui` has no test files outside `extensions/` (confirmed: 30/30 are under `extensions/`).
- **Scope creep (low).** `packages/herdr` is explicitly out of scope (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); covering it would require re-litigating a closed won't-fix decision. Any further gap (e.g. a new package) becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption:** adding commands to `suiteCommands` (rather than only `groups`) is required, because `--type full` evidence resolves from `suiteCommands` only (evidence-path constraint). A group-only change would not satisfy AC2.

## Problem statement

The main checkout's local `dev` diverged from `origin/dev`, so `implement.py finish` skipped the post-push parent-branch sync and new worktrees forked from a stale base. The divergence itself is resolved; what remains is to record the resolution decision, capture the mechanism that now prevents a stale fork, and route the one still-live defect (changed-scope base resolution) to the repository that owns it.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — call `implement.py start` / `finish` and depend on a current fork base and a working post-push parent-branch sync. *As an implementation agent, I want a fresh worktree to fork from a base that is on `origin/dev`, so my changed-scope test selection measures my diff only.*
- **Operators / producers** — need an auditable answer to "what happened to the local commits that were not on `origin/dev`?" *As an operator, I want the `d1061add` outcome recorded with evidence, so a later audit does not re-open the question.*

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — `d1061add` decision recorded.** The work item records the decision *"treated as stale; local `dev` restored"* together with this evidence: `dev` reflog entry `7beb2841 dev@{2026-11-05 13:58:27 +0000}: reset: moving to origin/dev`; `git for-each-ref --contains d1061add` returns nothing (dangling object); the extraction re-landed on `dev` as `e0f81241 WL-0MW0KDZPM009TLL4`; `git cat-file -e origin/dev:src/commands/init.workflow.ts` succeeds; and `git diff --name-only 0af53651 d1061add` equals the file set of `git show --stat e0f81241` (`src/commands/init.ts`, `src/commands/init.workflow.ts`, `src/commands/init.sync.ts`, `tests/cli/init/init-workflow-sync-modules.test.ts`) — i.e. the re-landed commit carries the same work. No publish/rebase/push of `d1061add` is performed.
- [ ] **AC2 — Divergence check reproduces clean.** After `git fetch origin dev` in the main checkout, `git rev-list --count dev..origin/dev` is `0` **and** `git rev-list --count origin/dev..dev` is `0`. (Verified during intake: both sides `33bd3a07`.)
- [ ] **AC3 — Stale-fork prevention mechanism documented and verified.** The item records that `implement.py start` step 6.5 (`_sync_parent_branch_locked()` → `_sync_parent_branch()`) fetches `origin/<parent>` and fast-forwards the shared local parent ref *before* `git worktree add --track -b <wl-branch> <path> <parent>`, including the documented fail-open reasons (`dirty_working_tree`, `fetch_failed`, `diverged`, `merge_failed`, `diverged_or_checked_out`), and that a fork therefore lands on a base that is on `origin/dev` whenever the refresh succeeds. Validation criterion: the cited code path and reason strings still exist at the cited locations on `dev` (`grep` evidence quoted in the item).
- [ ] **AC4 — Changed-scope base defect handed off.** The `_resolve_merge_base()` ref-name-vs-SHA defect is tracked in the repository that owns `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` as `SA-0MW3PBH00003HTAA` (SorraAgents store, `bug`/`medium`/`idea`), and this item links it. No edit is made to `~/.pi/agent/skills` (symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`) from this repository.
- [ ] **AC5 — Hygiene preserved.** The item performs no stash, no `git reset --hard`, and no force-push to `dev` or `main`. The 11 pre-existing orphaned stashes in the main checkout are explicitly out of scope (recorded as a follow-up opportunity, not worked here).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation and gate.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (for this record-only item: the item description itself is the artefact; no ContextHub doc describes the parent-branch sync path, verified by `grep -rln "commit_not_based_on_remote_tip\|local_dev_diverged\|sync_parent_branch" docs/` returning nothing). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes — no ContextHub code change is expected, so the dev-push gate run is the confirming evidence.

## Constraints

- **Scope is record-and-verify, not implementation.** Every observable defect found lives outside this repository (agent infrastructure in `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`), and a worktree cannot span repositories.
- `--merge`, never `--hard`, for any restoration of local `dev`; no force-push to `dev`/`main`; no stashing without explicit operator permission.
- Skill/infrastructure files (`~/.pi/agent/skills`, `skill/`) are read-only from this project — defects are reported via work items, not patched in place.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `dev` == `origin/dev` == `33bd3a07`; `d1061add` is dangling and referenced by no branch.
- `WL-0MW0KDZPM009TLL4` (Extract init workflow and sync modules) is `completed`/`in_review`; its extraction is on `dev` via `e0f81241` — `src/commands/init.workflow.ts`, `src/commands/init.sync.ts` and their test file `tests/cli/init/init-workflow-sync-modules.test.ts` present.
- The stale fork that produced the symptoms came from `1a4bb73`-era worktree state; `git worktree list` shows 5 registered worktrees plus 3 detached `/tmp/wl-*` check-outs (pre-existing).
- `run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` still `return candidate` (the ref name) instead of the `git merge-base` SHA — live defect, now tracked as `SA-0MW3PBH00003HTAA`.
- `git stash list` = 11 entries, all pre-existing (oldest from earlier items), untouched by this work.

## Desired change

A short, auditable closure record: the `d1061add` decision with reproduction commands, the divergence verification, the mechanism (and its fallback conditions) that stops new worktrees forking from a stale base, and a pointer to the upstream item that fixes changed-scope base resolution. No ContextHub source change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- *(none — no ContextHub source change)*

# Implement: thread uninitialised worklog notice into TUI

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — visible, persistent error instead of a silent blank list.** When no valid worklog root can be resolved for the pane's CWD, the selection-list TUI renders a persistent error line that names the uninitialised worklog (including the resolved path) and instructs the operator to run `wl init`. The pane must not render an empty list with no explanation. The line is re-rendered every frame while the state holds and disappears on a subsequent refresh once a valid worklog root is resolved.
- **AC2 — covers both missing and invalid `.worklog/`.** The error is shown whenever `resolveWorklogRoot()` returns `undefined`: a missing `.worklog/` and an existing but invalid `.worklog/` (for example only `worklog.db`, no `config.yaml`/`initialized`). It must not be shown when a valid root is resolved.
- **AC3 — canonical `wl init` wording; non-interactive diagnostic preserved.** Every user-facing uninitialised message uses the canonical command `wl init` (replacing the current `worklog init` text in `uninitializedReport()` and `formatWlError()`). The existing stderr diagnostic is retained for non-interactive / TUI-unavailable runs, using the same wording.
- **AC4 — testing/validation.** New or updated unit tests cover: (a) the error is present in the rendered output when the worklog root is unresolved and absent when it is resolved; (b) the explicit `wl init` wording; (c) the invalid/partial `.worklog/` case is treated as uninitialised. Tests live in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and the worklist renderer tests.

## Implementation Notes

- In `main()` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`): capture the start dir used for `configureWorklogTarget()`, and when `wlRoot` is `undefined`, call `uninitializedReport(startDir)` and pass the result to `runWorklistTui`.
- In `runWorklistTui` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`): add `uninitialisedNotice?: string | null` to the options type, store it, and pass it to `createListRenderer`.
- In `createListRenderer`: add the parameter and render the banner conditionally (when set AND displayRows is empty).
- Fix copy in `uninitializedReport()` (`packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts`) and `formatWlError()` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts`): `worklog init` → `wl init`.

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `main()` passes uninitialisedNotice to runWorklistTui.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts` — `uninitializedReport()` copy fix.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts` — `formatWlError()` copy fix.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` options + `createListRenderer` signature.

# Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run executed from the main checkout during post-push verification
can race with a sibling `implement.py finish` fast-forwarding the main
checkout's local `dev` (`git merge --ff-only`), swapping source files mid-run
and producing phantom failures (WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 evidence: 4 failures in
`tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` / `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` at
1abe9618; identical tree green in an isolated worktree minutes earlier).

## Goal (User Story)

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
2. The post-push verification path (and the audit skill F3 cache-miss
   auto-execution path) resolves an isolated worktree for the commit being
   verified and executes the full suite there — not in the live main checkout
   where a sibling `finish` can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
3. The fresh cache entry produced by the isolated-worktree run is grafted into
   the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` before/mirroring the pre-push hook's
   `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrites an existing entry), so
   read-only post-push verification and audits serve the grafted entry.
4. The mitigation is minimal and localised: document + redirect test execution
   to worktrees; it does not rewrite the post-push verification pipeline or
   change verdict semantics (`green`/`red`/`missing`/`not_applicable`).
5. The single-owner main-checkout flock lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) and the
   main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) remain intact; finish refuses
   loudly rather than masking a real failure.
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish()` read-only
  verification step and Step-6 main-checkout dev fast-forward
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_tests_via_test_skill` /
  F3 auto-execution (`run_cached(..., cwd=per_audit_root)`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` — suite execution
  and cache
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — guidance to match

## Constraints

- Must not break the dev-push pre-push hook's cache mirroring
  (`mirror_suite_cache`, `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` in ContextHub /
  `.githooks/pre-push`).
- The audit skill's F3 cache-miss path must be covered (audits running in the
  main checkout face the same race).
- Worktree creation cost is assumed negligible (node_modules is symlinked);
  latency must stay bounded.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

# Suppress known phantom test-failure patterns in triage

## Problem Statement

When the main checkout's `dev` is fast-forwarded mid-test-run by a sibling
`implement.py finish`, a suite produces failures that exist in **no single
commit** (tests from X, source from Y). The test-failure triage logic can mint
phantom `test-failure` work items from such mixed-tree output, creating noise
and false work for producers (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a producer, I want the triage logic to detect and suppress known phantom
patterns (mixed-tree verdicts from a moving checkout) so they no longer
auto-mint critical `test-failure` work items, while genuine failures still
triage normally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No phantom test-failure items:** after the mitigation, the race no longer
   generates additional phantom test-failure work items without manual triage;
   existing test-failure triage logic detects and suppresses known phantom
   patterns.
2. The test-failure triage helper detects known phantom signatures — a
   `state_changed_during_run` / mid-run fast-forward flag, or output recorded
   while the executing checkout was not a stable, pinned tree — and suppresses
   auto-creation of a `test-failure` work item, recording the suppression
   reason instead.
3. A suppressed phantom is still reported in the run's output/report with an
   explicit notice (`state_changed_during_run` notice code or equivalent),
   so the information is never silently lost — it is simply not minted as a
   critical item.
4. A genuine failure on a stable checkout still creates/updates a
   `test-failure` work item exactly as before (no behaviour change for real
   failures).
5. The suppression is covered by tests (both a phantom pattern that is
   suppressed and a genuine failure that is triaged).
6. The full project test suite passes with the change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — the triage helper
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` —
  `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage` / `_post_push_failure_test_name`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — F3 `_run_tests_via_test_skill`
  triage routing
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py` —
  `state_changed_during_run` notice

## Constraints

- Existing triage behaviour for real failures must be preserved.
- Inverse: suppression must be conservative — never suppress when the failure
  may be genuine.
- Implementation repo: framework skills live in the SorraAgents repo
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`); run
  `wl` worktree-safely with `--worklog-dir` when operating there.

# Implement: hasPeerOffer liveness-aware predicate

Parent AC7 (option A, producer-confirmed 2026-11-06): peer offers older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` count as absent peers so the leader is never held back by a dead instance's stale entry. Entry expiry (`pruneStaleEntries`) remains a deliberate no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `hasPeerOffer` is made liveness-aware (rejects entries older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`), and the decision is recorded in code comments and docs; entry expiry remains a no-op (parent AC7).
- `hasPeerOffer(entries, instanceId)` gains additive optional `nowMs`/`staleMs` parameters (default `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`); an entry whose `lastUpdated` is older than the window is treated as no peer (AC7).
- Both call sites (orchestrator-tick, orchestrator-dispatch) pass their live clock; fresh-entry behaviour is unchanged (no cooldown-cancellation regression).
- `pruneStaleEntries` remains a no-op: returns 0 and never mutates the coordination file.
- The conservative decision rationale (stale = absent peer makes the leader more willing to sweep, never less) is recorded in code comments; heartbeat/peer-liveness broadcasts stay out of scope (scope-creep guard).
- Liveness suite (T2) is green; full project test suite must pass with the new changes (AC11).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — predicate
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` — call site 1
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — call site 2
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts` — T2 spec

## Dependencies

Depends on T2 (test-first contract).

Liveness-aware predicate, green against T2, decision documented.
